name: Asaph
description: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed to sound cymbals of brass; others played harps and psalteries; the priests blew the trumpets before the ark, and doorkeepers were set. Every rank had its assigned place.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

points: Asaph was made chief, with named Levites playing psalteries, harps, and cymbals, and priests sounding trumpets continually. No one could take another's job or the whole order would fail.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: David delivered this psalm into the hand of Asaph to thank the Most High, a prayer for the congregation much like a set brother who sends up the prayers.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: David left Asaph and his brethren before the ark to minister continually, as every day's work required, with Obededom and doorkeepers appointed.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: David and the captains of the host separated to the service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, psalteries, and cymbals. Music is a form of prophecy. Miriam, when she came out, prophesied with the women, leading them in prophecy which was with music.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 25: The Singers and Musicians of the Sanctuary

points: All these were under the hands of their father for song in the house of the Lord with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of God, according to the king's order. Just as with Asaph, all the sons were doing the same thing the father did; if he was a musician, his son was a musician, kept in the family.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 25: The Singers and Musicians of the Sanctuary

points: The first lot came forth for Asaph to Joseph, the second to Gedaliah, and so on through the twenty and four courses of the singers, each with his sons and his brethren being twelve. The number twelve is mentioned on purpose, patterned after the twelve tribes of Israel, as many things in the temple order are done with the twelve tribes in mind.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 25: The Singers and Musicians of the Sanctuary

points: When the priests came out of the holy place, the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun with their sons and brethren, stood arrayed in white linen with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, and a hundred and twenty priests sounded with trumpets.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: The king and princes command the Levites to sing praise with the words of David and Asaph the seer, and they sing with gladness and bow their heads in worship.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

points: The singers, the sons of Asaph, are in their place according to the commandment of David, and the porters wait at every gate so they need not depart from their service.

Truly God is good to Israel, to such as are of a clean heart. Asaph's feet had almost slipped, because he was envious at the foolish when he saw the prosperity of the wicked. Some of us in here get envious the same way.

O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old. We are his congregation. This psalm of Asaph is prophecy of Babylon overthrowing Jerusalem, and Rome as well: thine enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time
